analysis.title: Whirlpool Corp. (WHR): 3Q26 First Take
key_insights: Whirlpool reported 3Q26 adj. EPS of ($0.21) vs GS estimate of $1.02 and FactSet consensus of $0.73. The adj. EBIT margin was 2.6%, 241bps below the GS forecast, a ($1.17) impact on EPS. Revenue fell 9% vs GS estimate of -2%, a ($0.16) impact.
Other EPS bridge items vs GS estimate: higher convertible preferred stock dividend ($0.08), other items +$0.14, interest expense +$0.05.

GS attributes the miss to a deceleration in demand that hit volume and mix, along with rising inflation. This is consistent with a moderating housing market and lower consumer confidence. Whirlpool's North America share was flat.
Whirlpool is realizing recently announced pricing and productivity initiatives. Freight and raw material cost increases are offsetting them.
2026 guidance was cut: sales guide lowered by 3% and adj. EBIT margin guide by about 190bps. Full-year adj. EPS outlook is about ($1.30) vs GS forecast of $1.70 and consensus of $1.21.
Management announced a 7+% price increase in MDA North America and Latin America, effective in December, to offset persistent inflation.

North America MDA sales fell 8.3% YoY vs GS estimate of +1.0%. GS estimates volumes grew 2.2% in 3Q25, a tough comp. Mix headwinds intensified and price realization continued. The decline was well below 3Q AHAM T-6 shipments of -3.3%.
North America adj. segment EBIT margin was 3.0%, 222bps below GS forecast and down about 200bps YoY. Pricing and structural cost take-out were offset by lost operating leverage, mix and inflation.

Latin America revenue rose 6.9% (+2.5% ex FX) vs GS estimate of +10%, led by volume. Adj. EBIT margin was 2.0%, 366bps below GS model, on negative mix after Grupo Casas Bahia's bankruptcy reorganization.

Small Domestic Appliance revenue fell 0.7% (-0.9% ex FX) vs GS estimate of +10.9%, on strong sell-out and order timing. October in the US was up about 40% YOY. Segment margin was 18.6%, 260bps above GS model and up about 210bps YOY.

Net debt/EBITDA reached 8.0x, up from 7.5x sequentially and 5.7x a year ago, with $1.1bn cash. 3Q FCF was $28mn. The 2026 FCF guide of about $300mn is largely unchanged, including about $700mn CFO and $150mn from timing of inventory shifts in Brazil. WHR expects net debt below $4.5bn by year-end.
GS is Neutral on WHR with a 12-month price target of $41, based on 7.2x its Q5-Q8 adj. EBITDA estimate. The stock closed at $26.45 on 26 Oct 2026, implying 55.0% upside to the target.

Questions GS will ask on the call: NA MDA volumes vs price/mix, mix and retail floor space, margin drivers, the timing of the 4Q SDA guide and 2027 expectations, Latin America conditions including Casas Bahia, and the 2027 deleveraging path and liquidity.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Neutral after a large 3Q EPS miss and a guidance cut. The $41 target is unchanged from the 12-Oct-26 note and is based on 7.2x Q5-Q8 adj. EBITDA.

sector_views.rationale: Demand is decelerating with housing moderation and weaker consumer confidence. Inflation in freight and raw materials is pressuring margins even as pricing and productivity actions take hold.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 (reported 10/26/26): adj. EPS ($0.21) reported vs GS estimate $1.02 and FactSet consensus $0.73.
3Q26 adj. EBIT margin 2.6% reported, 241bps below GS forecast. Revenue down 9% reported vs GS estimate of -2%.
FY2026 adj. EPS guide about ($1.30) (company outlook) vs GS estimate $1.70 and consensus $1.21. Sales guide lowered 3% and adj. EBIT margin guide lowered about 190bps.
GS FY2026E EPS is $1.70 (pre-print, not updated in this first take), with 12/27E $2.95 and 12/28E $4.25.
NA MDA segment: sales -8.3% YoY reported vs GS estimate +1.0%, adj. EBIT margin 3.0% reported.
LatAm: revenue +6.9% (+2.5% ex FX) reported, adj. EBIT margin 2.0% reported. SDA: revenue -0.7% (-0.9% ex FX) reported, adj. EBIT margin 18.6% reported.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Industry appliance shipments fell, but Whirlpool's NA MDA sales fell more (-8.3%), well below the industry figure.

risk_factors: Upside risks to Neutral: NA MDA price/mix beats expectations, trade-action benefits exceed expectations, cost-reduction initiatives deliver more profit, housing recovery lifts repair and remodel demand, dividends and shareholder returns resume from debt reduction.

Downside risks: rising competition limits pricing power and raises promotions, new products and strategic initiatives fail to gain traction, raw material cost inflation exceeds expectations with inability to pass costs through, and the impact of trade actions.
Leverage of 8.0x net debt/EBITDA with weak 3Q FCF of $28mn.
Latin America exposure to the Casas Bahia bankruptcy.
